# Bugs

This file uses [Prose form](../AGENTS.md#prose-form). It
lists known defects we're aware of but haven't scheduled a fix for.
Each entry describes what goes wrong, when, and the cost of
the failure. Entries are numbered (`1.` `2.` …) the same way
as `## Todo` in `../TODO.md`; run
`vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run notes/bugs.md` to renumber after
insert / delete / reorder.

## Bugs

1. 2t benches accept a 1-CPU pin pool and livelock through spin
   handoffs. `core_for` wraps the pin pool (`src/harness.rs`),
   so e.g. `iiac-perf zcr-mpsc-2t --pin 8` pins both the main
   thread and the spinning echo worker to core 8. Neither side
   yields, so every handoff waits for an involuntary preemption
   (milliseconds instead of ~200 ns) — the 5×1,000-step cost
   estimate alone takes minutes and the run appears hung.
   Observed on 3900x 2026-07-26; `--pin 8,9` behaves normally.
   Cost: an apparent hang the user must ^C, with no hint that
   the pinning was the cause. The bug requires pinning — an
   unpinned run lets the scheduler separate the threads and
   behaves normally. Fix direction:
   - Track `core_for` requests in `RunCfg` (max `thread_idx`
     asked for): thread placement only goes through `core_for`
     when pinning is active, so refusing a pool with fewer
     unique CPUs than requested placements covers every path
     to this bug — no per-bench thread-count declaration
     needed.
   - Independently, put a wall-clock deadline on the open-loop
     5×1,000-step estimate phase so *any* pathologically slow
     bench aborts with a diagnostic instead of hanging.

# References

Each entry describes what goes wrong, when, and the cost of
the failure. Entries are numbered (`1.` `2.` …) the same way
as `## Todo` in `../TODO.md`; run
`vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run notes/bugs.md` to renumber after
insert / delete / reorder.

## Bugs

1. 2t benches accept a 1-CPU pin pool and livelock through spin
   handoffs. `core_for` wraps the pin pool (`src/harness.rs`),
   so e.g. `iiac-perf zcr-mpsc-2t --pin 8` pins both the main
   thread and the spinning echo worker to core 8. Neither side
   yields, so every handoff waits for an involuntary preemption
   (milliseconds instead of ~200 ns) — the 5×1,000-step cost
   estimate alone takes minutes and the run appears hung.
   Observed on 3900x 2026-07-26; `--pin 8,9` behaves normally.
   Cost: an apparent hang the user must ^C, with no hint that
   the pinning was the cause. The bug requires pinning — an
   unpinned run lets the scheduler separate the threads and
   behaves normally. Fix direction:
   - Track `core_for` requests in `RunCfg` (max `thread_idx`
     asked for): thread placement only goes through `core_for`
     when pinning is active, so refusing a pool with fewer
     unique CPUs than requested placements covers every path
     to this bug — no per-bench thread-count declaration
     needed.
   - Independently, put a wall-clock deadline on the open-loop
     5×1,000-step estimate phase so *any* pathologically slow
     bench aborts with a diagnostic instead of hanging.

Thoughts — I like it, and I'd slot it *later*, into the blocks-first-class cycle rather than now:

**The case for it.** The summary rows currently inherit the band table's column geometry: the `mean` label sits at the left margin and its value lands ~80 columns away, right-aligned under the table's `mean` column. That alignment was deliberate (the values read as a continuation of the column above them), but the eye-tracking cost is real, and it gets worse the wider the table is — `--decimals 3` runs are exactly where you've been squinting. A `Results:` block styled like `Setup:` — label, two spaces, value — kills that span, and the Setup/Results symmetry gives the report a clean narrative frame: inputs at the top, raw distribution in the middle, conclusions at the bottom.

**What it touches.** More than a format tweak: `qualify` parses the report's mean row for its table, so the parser follows; README's worked examples all show the current shape; and the open design question is whether the grade block moves *inside* Results (it is results) or stays its own section (it has its own header row and the parser lives there too — my lean is keep it separate, `Results:` holding the scalar summaries only). There's also a small decision about whether the trimmed row and blocks rows keep their compound labels (`mean p10..n2`, `mean blocks`) or get grouped sub-lines.

**Why later, not now.** The blocks entry (#2) already commits to reworking exactly these rows — CI95/LSC always printing, `-` below the display gate. Doing the `Results:` re-house in the same pass means one parser update, one README example refresh, and one review of the new surface instead of two. content.text:
Both are good instincts; here are the mechanics and trade-offs.

**The bookend naming.** The pairing convention is genuinely useful — `git log --grep "dynamic warmup"` collects the cycle, and open/close read as brackets. Two wrinkles:

- *Type honesty*: the opening commit is bookkeeping, which is why it's currently `chore:`. `feat: dynamic warmup opening` types it as a feature it isn't. `chore: dynamic warmup opening` + `feat: dynamic warmup` keeps the pair visually adjacent (shared stem, grep still works) while keeping conventional-commit types truthful. Your call — the pairing matters more than the type pedantry, I just want it to be a decision.
- *The rewrite cost*: -0 is *published* (it's on `dynamic-warmup@origin` with an ochid). Retitling it is a hard-rule-4 event: `jj describe --ignore-immutable` with the ochid trailer hand-copied into the new message — allowed exactly because we're coordinating it here — plus every descendant rebases (all local, free), plus the records that carry the title verbatim must sync in the same breath: the chores-06 as-built rung line and TOC-adjacent mentions (which live inside the already-committed close-out commit, so that's a squash into it), and the eventual remote bookmark update becomes a force-push. All cheap on a topic branch — this is precisely the "free pre-landing rewrites" the bookmark exists for — but it's five moving pieces, not one.

**The trapezoid.** Your proposal has two possible readings and they differ in what gets ochid-stamped:

- *Reading A (what I'd recommend)*: publish the rungs to the bookmark per-rung with `vc-x1 push` as planned (each minted with its ochid, bot repo journaled per push), close-out pushed linearly as the last one — then, locally: rebase the close-out into the merge shape (`jj rebase -r <closeout> --onto <main-tip> --onto <rung-6>`; the rebase preserves its description *including the ochid trailer* — the 0.23.0 post-facto trapezoid proved this survives), point `main` at the merge, and `jj git push --bookmark main`. The merge shape itself never needs pushing to the bookmark remote — which I think may be what your "not pushed" means. The stale `dynamic-warmup@origin` gets force-synced or deleted afterwards as cleanup. Everything keeps its ochid; the landing is one ordinary (non-force) main push, since the merge's first parent is main's current tip.
- *Reading B (maximal "not pushed")*: skip all remaining bookmark pushes; build the trapezoid from the existing local chain, move main, push once. One push total — but `vc-x1 push` is the only thing that mints ochids and it has no commit-without-push mode, so the six rungs and close-out land on `main` with *no* ochid trailers at all (only the prep commit links to this conversation), and the bot repo needs one manual `vc-x1 squash-push -R .claude` at the end instead of its per-push cadence. Given rule 1's shape ("a rung is committed by vc-x1 push"), this is a real protocol deviation — survivable, single-user repo, but it's the biggest one we'd have made, and it's permanent in the published history.

One more detail either way: `vc-x1 push` must never be invoked *after* the merge is set up (the 0.22.0 empty-commit trap) — the main push is raw `jj git push`, and the SHA backfill for all the rungs happens after main lands, satisfying the topic-branch rule in one pass.

**My lean**: retitle -0 to `chore: dynamic warmup opening` (pairing with `feat: dynamic warmup`), adopt the bookend convention in custom.md for future cycles, and take Reading A — the bookmark-remote churn costs nothing, and it keeps every commit linked to its session and the bot journal on cadence. Reading B's one-push elegance is real, but it spends ochid coverage to buy it.

The plain version: renaming the opening commit is fine but touches five places because it's already published — doable, just done carefully. For the landing, there are two routes: publish each step to the side branch first and then fold the finish into a merge that main points at (keeps every commit traceable to this conversation), or skip straight to one merge and one push (cleanest history, but most of the commits lose their link back to the session records). I'd take the first route.

content.text:
Your grep argument holds up, and I'll concede the type-purity point without much fight.

On the search mechanics: the exact-pair search is actually even cleaner than you might expect, because of a hyphen accident — the rung titles in this cycle use the stem "warm", and the one nearby commit that mentions the concept (`docs: record the dynamic-warmup and placement-tracking designs`) spells it *hyphenated*, so a space-separated `"dynamic warmup"` already matches only the bookends. But that's luck, not design; as a *convention*, "both bookends share the identical `<type>: <name>` prefix" gives you one memorable pattern — `git log --grep "feat: dynamic warmup"` — that returns open and close and nothing else, every cycle, no cleverness with `": "` needed. Mixed types make the searcher think; identical types don't.

On the semantics: you're right that the chore/feat boundary is soft here, and the deciding fact is that nothing in this project *consumes* the type — versioning is scope-based per custom.md, there's no changelog generator keying off `feat:`. The only reader is a human scanning the log, and for that reader "feat: dynamic warmup opening ... feat: dynamic warmup" reads as exactly what it is: the start and finish of one feature's arc. The opening did open the feature — it published the design record and the ladder, which is feature work in the sense that matters. So `feat:` for both, and the pedantry loses.

One residual worth noting: after the trapezoid lands, the trunk's `--first-parent` view shows only the close-out merge — the opening lives on the side leg. So the bookends pair up in the full log and on the bookmark, not on the trunk skim. That doesn't weaken the convention; it just says its audience is the person spelunking a cycle, which is exactly who needs the bookends.

If we adopt it, the convention line for custom.md (and eventually the template) would be: *the opening commit's title is the close-out title plus " opening", same type; rungs keep their own titles on the shared stem.* Applied here: retitle -0 to `feat: dynamic warmup opening` — the published-commit rewrite we discussed, with the ochid hand-copy and the chores-06 record sync riding along.

55	Rather than K agreeing floors, grade a *sliding window* over
56	the warmup probe series and warm until the trailing window
57	reads A, or the cap (design 2026-07-28). The exit condition and
58	the warmup letter become one computation:
59	
60	- exit on A means the run started post-ramp by construction
61	- hitting the cap reports whatever the window actually scored,
62	  the "run started unstable" signal, not a silent proceed
63	- window length takes the same "minimum count or minimum wall
64	  time, whichever is larger" shape as pass length: count
65	  because the split detector needs 4 points a side, wall time
66	  because the ramp is a ms-scale phenomenon
67	- signals: spread, drift, step; `interference` is the weak one

74	Floors, not means, so one preemption doesn't fake

Rung -1 is landed and the chain is rebased onto it. Status and the corrected mechanics picture for when you're back:

**Your understanding, adjusted in one spot**: it's `vc-x1 push` for *all* of them — the six rungs *and* the close-out, each restored into the working copy and pushed linearly to the bookmark, so every commit gets its ochid and the bot journal keeps cadence. `jj` enters only at the very end, and your last sentence had it exactly right: once the linear chain is fully published and we're happy, we make the trapezoid on the working branch (`jj rebase` of the close-out into a merge — its description and ochid survive, per the 0.23.0 precedent), move `main` to it, and `jj git push --bookmark main` — one ordinary push, completely separate from the bookmark pushes. (`vc-x1 push` must never run after the merge exists — that's the 0.22.0 empty-commit trap.)

**Also done**: the bookend convention is in custom.md, -0 is retitled `feat: dynamic warmup opening` (ochid hand-copied, chores rung line synced into the close-out commit), and the -1 push initially tripped over the local bookmark pointing at the old scratch chain — recovered (orphan abandoned, bookmark repositioned, stale push state cleared) and the re-run went through all stages. That bookmark dance is now part of the known recipe; the remaining pushes won't hit it since the bookmark rides the published chain.

**Awaiting your go — the five remaining rung descriptions** (close-out's was already reviewed; -6's likewise, both reused verbatim):

**-2** `feat: warm until the trailing window grades A`
```
The dynamic exit lands: warm until the trailing probe window
grades A, or a hard cap, with the warmup pass doubling as the
sizing pass. The exit condition, the printed warmup letter, and
the graded tail are one computation over one window.

- Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock: version 0.24.0-1 -> 0.24.0-2
- src/harness.rs
  - WarmPass::Adaptive (min steps + min wall span, deadline
    capped, doubling check chunk); warm_loop returns per-pass
    step costs and feeds the exit test the probe series
  - warm_window (>= 8 probes and >= 50 ms suffix), WarmExit
    (Settled / Unstable / Uncertified), classify_warm
  - the exit window replaces the fixed 300 ms tail
    (WARMUP_TAIL_SECONDS deleted); env_stretches takes the
    recorded window; RunOutput carries warm_exit + warm_tail
  - sizing fusion: estimate_step_cost deleted; pick_inner
    reads the exit window's best pass
  - settle cell answers by exit verdict; -v per-probe table
  - tests reworked to the window semantics
- TODO.md: rung marked done
- notes/chores/chores-06.md: as-built rung + design notes
```

**-3** `feat: warm where the bench runs`
```
Main pins only when --pin is given (to the pool's first slot,
where it warms and measures); the CPU0-default tick-rate warm
pin and --no-pin-cal are deleted.

- Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock: version 0.24.0-2 -> 0.24.0-3
- src/main.rs: pin main to pin[0] iff --pin; --no-pin-cal
  removed; Setup cell renamed warm pin -> main pin
- src/pin.rs: save_affinity / restore_affinity deleted
- README.md: warm-pin surfaces reworked (five spots)
- TODO.md: rung marked done
- notes/chores/chores-06.md: as-built note
```

**-4** `feat: read the clock during warmup`
```
The exit gains its second gate: the delivered clock must hold
still across the exit window, separating "settled at the top"
from a dwell one P-state below it (the measured 7600x case; a
dwell is steady, so no timing test can).

- Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock: version 0.24.0-3 -> 0.24.0-4
- src/freq.rs (new): cpuinfo_avg_freq on the calling thread's
  CPU; scaling_cur_freq deliberately not a fallback
- src/harness.rs
  - one clock sample per warmup probe, aligned across the
    process-warm handoff; clock_stable (1% band, same CPU;
    anything less falls back to timing-only)
  - classify_warm: timing-A with a moving clock is Unstable
  - the -v summary line reports clock end/max MHz + ratio
- src/main.rs: mod freq
- TODO.md: rung marked done
- notes/chores/chores-06.md: as-built notes
```

**-5** `feat: settle follows the warm window grade`
```
Settle time becomes the earliest suffix of the warm stretch
that grades A, so the letter and the settle cell are one
computation and cannot disagree ("A + not settled" retired).

- Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock: version 0.24.0-4 -> 0.24.0-5
- src/gauge.rs: settle(warm, tail_len) scans suffix starts
  front-to-back, never shorter than the exit window;
  SETTLE_TOL, SETTLE_WINDOW, window_floors deleted
- src/harness.rs: callers pass the window length; tests
  updated
```

When you're back: one "go" can cover pushing all five plus -6 and close-out unattended (I'll report each as it lands and stop before the trapezoid for your review of the final shape), or we can go one at a time — your call. Enjoy dinner.
